headline: State desk: Massachusetts seeks hemp oversight; Utah eyes open list
dek: Massachusetts regulators voted to seek control of intoxicating hemp, a Utah panel wants doctors free to recommend cannabis for any condition.
key_points: Massachusetts' Cannabis Control Commission voted unanimously on 17 November to approve a report saying it should regulate intoxicating hemp products; draft rules are due on 10 December.
The commission must send its recommendations to lawmakers by 15 December, four days after the federal hemp THC cap is due.
A Utah advisory committee made any-condition recommendations a top priority for the 2027 session; the state now lists 16 qualifying conditions.
Illinois is seeking a contractor for at least 24 medical cannabis training sessions; bids close on 30 November.
body: Three states moved this week on the edges of their cannabis programmes: who regulates hemp-derived THC, who decides which patients qualify, and who teaches doctors how the system works. None of the three is final. Each sets up a decision for legislators in the coming months.

The most immediate is in Massachusetts, where the Cannabis Control Commission (CCC) agreed on Tuesday 17 November that it should take charge of intoxicating hemp-derived cannabinoid products, MJBizDaily reported, citing The Boston Globe. The vote came at the same meeting where the commission cleared drive-through sales, which we covered on 17 November.
## Massachusetts: the commission wants intoxicating hemp

The commission voted unanimously to approve a report on regulating the hemp-derived cannabinoid market, according to MJBizDaily. The report responds to a recent state cannabis law that told the CCC to study that market and recommend rules on licensing, testing, age limits and retail sales, after years in which intoxicating hemp products fell between regulators.

The plan separates two kinds of product. Intoxicating hemp-derived products would come under the CCC. Non-intoxicating hemp products would move through the commission's regulated cannabis supply chain and could be sold both inside and outside licensed cannabis shops. Selling them outside licensed retailers would need a change in the law, the outlet reported. The Department of Agricultural Resources would keep oversight of hemp growing.

Commissioner Xiomara DeLobato said the change could open a new revenue stream for licensed cannabis businesses and build brand recognition for those that make non-intoxicating hemp products, according to the Globe's account as relayed by MJBizDaily. Staff are due to present draft regulations at the commission's meeting on 10 December. The CCC has until 15 December to send its recommendations to state lawmakers.
> Massachusetts is writing state hemp rules on a timetable that ends four days after the federal cap is due to remove most of the products.

The timing is tight. The federal limit of 0.4 milligrams of total THC per container is due to take effect on 11 December unless Congress acts, a day after the CCC sees its draft rules. If the federal cap arrives, the commission's intoxicating-hemp category would cover products that federal law treats as marijuana. If Congress delays or replaces it, Massachusetts would have a state framework ready. Either way the legislature, not the commission, decides.
## Utah: let providers decide

In Utah, the Industry Committee of the state's Medical Cannabis Policy Advisory Board has proposed letting medical providers recommend cannabis for any condition they think it could help, The Marijuana Herald reported from the board's meeting documents. The committee placed the idea in its highest-priority group for the 2027 legislative session.

Utah now recognises 16 qualifying conditions, among them cancer, epilepsy, multiple sclerosis, post-traumatic stress disorder, autism and some forms of persistent pain. A patient with a condition outside the list generally has to apply to the state's Compassionate Use Board, which reviews cases one by one. The committee wants providers to have discretion for conditions such as sleep disturbance, generalised anxiety disorder and major depressive disorder, according to the Herald.

The same top-priority group includes wider telehealth access, extending medical cannabis cards from one year to two, and changes to licensing rules for some processors. At the board meeting, members and state officials raised questions about data collection, provider education and how lawmakers would react, the Herald reported. A separate, narrower proposal to add sleep disorders to the list was also discussed. Any of these changes needs an act of the legislature.

For Utah's operators, the proposal matters more than its modest wording suggests. A closed list caps the patient pool; provider discretion removes the cap and puts the limit on clinical judgement. A two-year card would also cut renewal visits in half. These are an industry committee's recommendations to an advisory board, so they are two steps from a bill.
## Illinois: training for doctors and patients

Illinois' Department of Public Health has issued a request for proposals for a contractor to build and run a statewide medical cannabis education programme, the Herald reported. The state listing shows the solicitation on Illinois' BidBuy procurement site.

The contractor must hold at least 12 training sessions for health care providers, with a minimum of 15 participants each, and another 12 for patients, caregivers and the public, with at least 25 each, during the initial contract period. That is a floor of 180 provider places and 300 public places, on our arithmetic. All participating local health departments, eight at present, would also be trained. Sessions can be online, in person or mixed.

Training would cover the state's Medical Cannabis Patient Registry System, the laws and rules of the programme, and standards of care. The contractor must complete a needs assessment in the first six months. The initial contract runs 18 months with three optional one-year extensions. Proposals are due on 30 November, the award is expected on 24 February 2027 and the contract is expected to start on 1 July 2027, according to the Herald.

The department said it now does this work with internal staff and limited structured activity. The solicitation arrives in the same week that a federal judge declined to block the Illinois Hemp Act, which sends hemp-derived THC products over 0.4 milligrams into licensed dispensaries, as we report separately today.
## What to watch

On 10 December the Massachusetts commission sees draft hemp regulations; on 15 December its recommendations are due at the legislature. On 30 November Illinois closes bids for its training contract. Utah's 2027 legislative session will show whether any lawmaker takes up the any-condition proposal, the two-year card or the telehealth change.
